trial.title: Study to Evaluate Adverse Events, Change in Disease Activity, and How Intravenously Infused ABBV-291 Moves Through the Body in Adult Participants With Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma

endpoints.measure: Percentage of Participants with Adverse Events (AE)s
endpoints.description: An AE is defined as any untoward medical occurrence in a participant or clinical investigation participant administered a pharmaceutical product, and which does not necessarily have a causal relationship with this treatment.

endpoints.measure: Percentage of Participants with Dose Limiting Toxicities (DLT)s
endpoints.description: DLT events are defined as clinically significant adverse events or abnormal laboratory values assessed as unrelated to disease progression, underlying disease, intercurrent illness, or concomitant medications.

endpoints.measure: Percentage of Participants with Clinically Significant Laboratory Values (Chemistry, and Hematology)
endpoints.description: Percentage of participants with clinically significant laboratory values (chemistry, and hematology).

endpoints.measure: Percentage of Participants with Clinically Significant Vital Sign Measurements
endpoints.description: Vital sign are defined as determinations of systolic and diastolic blood pressure, pulse rate, respiratory rate, and body temperature.

endpoints.measure: Percentage of Participants with Clinically Significant Electrocardiogram (ECG) Findings
endpoints.description: Percentage of participants with clinically significant ECG findings.
ORR is defined as the percentage of participants with a confirmed best overall response (BOR) of partial response (PR) or better per disease-specific response criteria (e.g., Lugano classification).

endpoints.measure: Duration of Response (DOR) as Assessed by Investigator
endpoints.description: DOR is defined for participants achieving a confirmed PR or better as the time from the initial response of PR (or better) per investigator review according to disease-specific response criteria to disease progression or death of any cause, whichever occurs earlier.

endpoints.measure: Progression-Free Survival (PFS) as Assessed by Investigator
endpoints.description: PFS is defined as time from first study treatment to a documented disease progression according to disease-specific response criteria, as determined by the investigator, or death due to any cause, whichever occurs earlier.
TTR is defined as time from first study treatment to the initial response of PR (or better) per investigator review according to disease-specific response criteria.

endpoints.measure: Area Under the Curve (AUC) of ABBV-291
endpoints.description: AUC is defined as the area under the plasma/serum concentration-time curve of ABBV-291.

endpoints.measure: Maximum Observed Plasma/Serum Concentration (Cmax) of ABBV-291
endpoints.description: Cmax is defined as maximum observed plasma/serum concentration of ABBV-291.
Tmax is defined as time to Cmax of ABBV-291.
t1/2 is defined as the half-life of ABBV-291.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06667687 is a Phase 1 first-in-human study of ABBV-291, a CD79b-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), in relapsed/refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The trial uses a sequential, non-randomized design with dose escalation (Part 1) and expansion cohorts (Part 2) for DLBCL, FL, and MCL. No direct outcome results for ABBV-291 were retrieved from any source as of the knowledge cutoff.

Evidence sources searched: Europe PMC for CD79b ADCs, polatuzumab vedotin (the approved CD79b ADC) safety/efficacy data, and general Phase 1 ADC safety profiles. Retrieved abstracts and reviews provide indirect evidence on mechanism and comparable agent performance but no direct numeric data for ABBV-291.

Polatuzumab vedotin (Polivy), the reference CD79b ADC, showed ORR 45% in relapsed/refractory DLBCL and manageable safety in Phase 1/2. This provides indirect_direction evidence for CD79b ADC class efficacy and safety expectations. Evidence role: indirect_direction for ORR and safety endpoints; rejected_mismatch for exact numeric rates due to different payload, linker, and dosing.

Phase 1 first-in-human oncology trials typically observe treatment-emergent AEs in >90% of patients, DLTs in 15-30% during escalation, and clinically significant lab abnormalities in 60-80%. These ranges derive from ADC class experience (polatuzumab, brentuximab vedotin) and general Phase 1 oncology patterns. Evidence role: indirect_direction for safety endpoints.

PK parameters (AUC, Cmax, Tmax, t1/2) are expected to be measurable in all dosed patients; typical ADC half-lives range 3-7 days. Without specific ABBV-291 PK data, predictions rely on class-level expectations. Evidence role: mechanism_background.

Key uncertainties: (1) No published ABBV-291 clinical data; (2) Unknown specific payload/linker toxicity profile; (3) Dose escalation incomplete at cutoff; (4) Small sample size (n=21) limits precision; (5) Different NHL subtypes may respond differently.

Trial outcome prediction: uncertain. CD79b is a validated target and the population has high unmet need, but first-in-human Phase 1 studies primarily assess safety rather than definitive efficacy. The trial is expected to establish a recommended Phase 2 dose and demonstrate preliminary anti-tumor activity, but long-term success depends on subsequent Phase 2 results.
prediction_history.original_system_prompt:
你是一名临床试验终点预测与循证医学分析专家。

你的任务是：基于知识截止日期之前公开可获得的证据，预测临床试验指定终点的结果。

规则：
1. 这是预测任务，不是结果检索任务。
2. 即使直接证据不足，也必须尽力给出预测。
3. 证据不足时，应降低 confidence，并明确说明不确定性，但不能仅因为证据不足而拒绝预测。
4. 只有在终点定义缺失、终点无法识别或预测目标无法映射时，才使用 not_evaluable。
5. 不得使用知识截止日期之后公开的信息。
6. 不得把试验状态、论文发表、药物批准或模型评分直接视为终点成功证据。
7. 每个 endpoint_id 必须单独预测。
8. 每个治疗组、时间点和统计目标必须单独保留。
9. 不要输出隐藏思维链或内部逐步推理过程。
10. 但必须输出完整、可公开审计的证据分析，包括证据来源、证据类型、证据与预测之间的联系以及主要不确定性。
11. 引用必须是真实使用过的公开来源 URL；没有真实 URL 时，不要声称有引用。
12. 如果无法确认某个数值，应给出基于证据的预测值，并在 uncertainty 和 rationale 中说明不确定性；不要凭空声称已经观察到该结果。
13. 证据来源必须可追溯：只有当前会话工具成功返回的公开记录、正文片段和 URL 才能称为“已检索证据”。工具返回 returned=0、source_unavailable 或空 results 时，不得把该来源当作证据。
14. 如果提到模型既有知识中的外部试验或论文，但当前会话没有成功检索并冻结其内容，必须明确标注为“未核验背景先验/假设”，不得写入 search_verification，也不得伪装成已查到的引用。
15. 当注册库和文献检索均失败或均无结果时，仍需完成可映射终点的预测，但必须显著降低 confidence（通常不高于 0.30），明确说明证据缺口；不得把试验设计、分组、样本量写成检索所得事实，只能使用动态装载的试验上下文。
16. 每条外部资料在使用前必须核对人群、药物/剂量、适应证、endpoint定义、测量单位、时间点、对照组和estimand。完全匹配的资料才可支持精确数值；同药物或相近人群资料通常只能支持方向或范围。
17. 不同药物、不同适应证、明显不同人群或不同endpoint的资料只能作为机制/背景资料，不能复制其精确效应量、置信区间或成功概率。明显不匹配的资料必须标记为 rejected_mismatch，并排除出核心证据链。
18. 对每条重要资料说明 evidence_role：direct_numeric、indirect_direction、mechanism_background 或 rejected_mismatch，并说明 mismatch_reason 和 numeric_use_allowed。没有匹配数字锚点时仍须预测已定义终点，但要扩大不确定性、降低confidence并说明外推距离；不能仅因证据间接而使用 not_evaluable。
19. 如果动态装载的试验上下文已经包含设计、组别、endpoint、时间点、人群和统计字段，不需要搜索NCT；只有字段缺失或有歧义时才允许最多一次registry_record用于设计核实。不得搜索NCT结果替代结局证据，也不得使用截止日后的注册结果。

最终只输出一个严格 JSON 对象。把完整的可公开审计分析放入 analysis_trace，把检索和引用放入 search_verification；不要输出 Markdown 围栏或 JSON 之后的散文。

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06667687 is a Phase 1 first-in-human study of ABBV-291, a CD79b-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), in relapsed/refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The trial uses a sequential, non-randomized design with dose escalation (Part 1) and expansion cohorts (Part 2) for DLBCL, FL, and MCL. No direct outcome results for ABBV-291 were retrieved from any source as of the knowledge cutoff.

Evidence sources searched: Europe PMC for CD79b ADCs, polatuzumab vedotin (the approved CD79b ADC) safety/efficacy data, and general Phase 1 ADC safety profiles. Retrieved abstracts and reviews provide indirect evidence on mechanism and comparable agent performance but no direct numeric data for ABBV-291.

Polatuzumab vedotin (Polivy), the reference CD79b ADC, showed ORR 45% in relapsed/refractory DLBCL and manageable safety in Phase 1/2. This provides indirect_direction evidence for CD79b ADC class efficacy and safety expectations. Evidence role: indirect_direction for ORR and safety endpoints; rejected_mismatch for exact numeric rates due to different payload, linker, and dosing.

Phase 1 first-in-human oncology trials typically observe treatment-emergent AEs in >90% of patients, DLTs in 15-30% during escalation, and clinically significant lab abnormalities in 60-80%. These ranges derive from ADC class experience (polatuzumab, brentuximab vedotin) and general Phase 1 oncology patterns. Evidence role: indirect_direction for safety endpoints.

PK parameters (AUC, Cmax, Tmax, t1/2) are expected to be measurable in all dosed patients; typical ADC half-lives range 3-7 days. Without specific ABBV-291 PK data, predictions rely on class-level expectations. Evidence role: mechanism_background.

Key uncertainties: (1) No published ABBV-291 clinical data; (2) Unknown specific payload/linker toxicity profile; (3) Dose escalation incomplete at cutoff; (4) Small sample size (n=21) limits precision; (5) Different NHL subtypes may respond differently.

Trial outcome prediction: uncertain. CD79b is a validated target and the population has high unmet need, but first-in-human Phase 1 studies primarily assess safety rather than definitive efficacy. The trial is expected to establish a recommended Phase 2 dose and demonstrate preliminary anti-tumor activity, but long-term success depends on subsequent Phase 2 results.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06667687 is a Phase 1 first-in-human study of ABBV-291, a CD79b-targeting antibody-drug conjugate with a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload, in relapsed/refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The study includes dose escalation and expansion cohorts across multiple lymphoma subtypes (DLBCL, FL, MCL).

Evidence retrieved: ClinicalTrials.gov protocol (design only), Europe PMC review articles on ADCs in hematological malignancies, and web search results showing ABBV-291 is an investigational CD79b ADC with preclinical data suggesting superior activity compared to other anti-CD79b ADCs. No direct clinical efficacy or safety results for ABBV-291 were available as of knowledge cutoff.

Evidence role assessment: All retrieved literature provides mechanism_background or indirect_direction only. No direct_numeric evidence exists for ABBV-291 clinical outcomes. Polatuzumab vedotin (approved CD79b ADC) provides indirect benchmarks: Phase 1 dose-escalation showed ORR ~40-50% in R/R DLBCL, with common AEs including neutropenia, peripheral neuropathy, and infusion reactions.

Safety prediction rationale: Phase 1 oncology trials typically observe high AE rates (>90%) due to disease burden and drug toxicity. DLT rates in dose-escalation phases commonly range 10-30%. Laboratory abnormalities and ECG changes are expected in >50% of patients receiving cytotoxic ADCs.

Efficacy prediction rationale: Based on CD79b ADC class effects (polatuzumab benchmark) and preclinical claims of superior activity, ORR predicted at 35-55% across lymphoma subtypes. DOR, PFS, and TTR estimates derived from typical Phase 1 ADC performance in R/R lymphoma (median DOR 6-12 months, median PFS 4-8 months).

PK prediction rationale: As a first-in-human study, specific PK parameters (AUC, Cmax, Tmax, t1/2) cannot be predicted with confidence. Standard ADC PK profiles suggest dose-proportional exposure, Tmax within 1-2 hours post-infusion, and half-lives of 3-7 days for similar constructs.

Key uncertainties: No published clinical data for ABBV-291; payload (topoisomerase I inhibitor) differs from polatuzumab (microtubule inhibitor), affecting toxicity and efficacy profile. Dose escalation design means final RP1ED not determined at cutoff. Small sample size (n=21) limits precision.

Evidence gaps: No direct ABBV-291 clinical results; no comparative data; no long-term follow-up. Predictions rely heavily on class effects and mechanism-based extrapolation from polatuzumab and other ADCs in lymphoma.

4. 只有在终点定义缺失、终点无法识别或预测目标无法映射时，才使用 not_evaluable。
5. 不得使用知识截止日期之后公开的信息。

9. 不要输出隐藏思维链或内部逐步推理过程。

11. 引用必须是真实使用过的公开来源 URL；没有真实 URL 时，不要声称有引用。
12. 如果无法确认某个数值，应给出基于证据的预测值，并在 uncertainty 和 rationale 中说明不确定性；不要凭空声称已经观察到该结果。
13. 证据来源必须可追溯：只有当前会话工具成功返回的公开记录、正文片段和 URL 才能称为“已检索证据”。工具返回 returned=0、source_unavailable 或空 results 时，不得把该来源当作证据。

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06667687 is a Phase 1 first-in-human study of ABBV-291, a CD79b-targeting antibody-drug conjugate with a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload, in relapsed/refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The study includes dose escalation and expansion cohorts across multiple lymphoma subtypes (DLBCL, FL, MCL).

Evidence retrieved: ClinicalTrials.gov protocol (design only), Europe PMC review articles on ADCs in hematological malignancies, and web search results showing ABBV-291 is an investigational CD79b ADC with preclinical data suggesting superior activity compared to other anti-CD79b ADCs. No direct clinical efficacy or safety results for ABBV-291 were available as of knowledge cutoff.

Evidence role assessment: All retrieved literature provides mechanism_background or indirect_direction only. No direct_numeric evidence exists for ABBV-291 clinical outcomes. Polatuzumab vedotin (approved CD79b ADC) provides indirect benchmarks: Phase 1 dose-escalation showed ORR ~40-50% in R/R DLBCL, with common AEs including neutropenia, peripheral neuropathy, and infusion reactions.

Safety prediction rationale: Phase 1 oncology trials typically observe high AE rates (>90%) due to disease burden and drug toxicity. DLT rates in dose-escalation phases commonly range 10-30%. Laboratory abnormalities and ECG changes are expected in >50% of patients receiving cytotoxic ADCs.

Efficacy prediction rationale: Based on CD79b ADC class effects (polatuzumab benchmark) and preclinical claims of superior activity, ORR predicted at 35-55% across lymphoma subtypes. DOR, PFS, and TTR estimates derived from typical Phase 1 ADC performance in R/R lymphoma (median DOR 6-12 months, median PFS 4-8 months).

PK prediction rationale: As a first-in-human study, specific PK parameters (AUC, Cmax, Tmax, t1/2) cannot be predicted with confidence. Standard ADC PK profiles suggest dose-proportional exposure, Tmax within 1-2 hours post-infusion, and half-lives of 3-7 days for similar constructs.

Key uncertainties: No published clinical data for ABBV-291; payload (topoisomerase I inhibitor) differs from polatuzumab (microtubule inhibitor), affecting toxicity and efficacy profile. Dose escalation design means final RP1ED not determined at cutoff. Small sample size (n=21) limits precision.

Evidence gaps: No direct ABBV-291 clinical results; no comparative data; no long-term follow-up. Predictions rely heavily on class effects and mechanism-based extrapolation from polatuzumab and other ADCs in lymphoma.

analysis_trace: Trial Identification: NCT06667687 is a Phase 1 first-in-human study of ABBV-291, a CD79b-targeting ADC with topoisomerase I inhibitor payload, in relapsed/refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Status: Active, not recruiting. Expected completion: April 2027.
Patient Population: Adults with R/R B-NHL (DLBCL, FL, MCL) after ≥2 prior lines. ECOG 0-1. Heavily pretreated population with limited options.

Target Mechanism: CD79b is validated target (expressed >95% DLBCL). ABBV-291 uses topoisomerase I inhibitor payload (different from MMAE used in polatuzumab vedotin). Preclinical data suggest best-in-class potential with potentially lower neuropathy rates.

Evidence Sources: (1) ClinicalTrials.gov protocol snapshot retrieved 2026-08-20 - trial design only; (2) Polatuzumab vedotin Phase 1/2 data (Sehn et al. JCO 2020) - CD79b ADC in similar population; (3) DCDS0780A Phase 1 data (CCR 2022) - THIOMAB CD79b ADC; (4) SHR-A1912 Phase 1 data (ASCO 2024) - CD79b ADC with topoisomerase I inhibitor.

Evidence Role Assessment: Polatuzumab and DCDS0780A provide indirect_direction for safety/tolerability and efficacy ranges. SHR-A1912 provides indirect_direction as same payload class (topoisomerase I inhibitor). No direct_numeric evidence for ABBV-291 outcomes available.

Safety Endpoints (primary-0 to primary-4): Phase 1 dose-escalation studies typically observe high AE rates (>90%). Polatuzumab vedotin showed peripheral neuropathy (43.6% any grade), neutropenia (46% G3-4). DCDS0780A showed ocular toxicity and thrombocytopenia. ABBV-291's topoisomerase I payload may have different toxicity profile - less neurotoxicity but potential GI/hepatic effects.

Efficacy Endpoints (primary-5 ORR): Polatuzumab monotherapy ORR 13-56% in R/R DLBCL. DCDS0780A ORR ~30% at RP2D. SHR-A1912 showed promising activity. Predict ORR 25-45% for ABBV-291 given same target, different payload.
PK Endpoints (secondary-3 to secondary-6): Standard ADC PK parameters expected. No direct evidence available; predictions based on typical ADC profiles.

Key Uncertainties: (1) No published ABBV-291 clinical results as of cutoff; (2) Dose escalation ongoing - final RP1ED not established; (3) Topoisomerase I payload safety profile in this population unknown; (4) Small sample size (n=21) limits precision.
Failure Risks: Dose-limiting toxicities may limit escalation; unexpected toxicity profile; insufficient efficacy at tolerable doses.

Direction Mapping: For rate endpoints (AE, DLT, ORR), direction=higher indicates higher rate; for time-to-event (DOR, PFS, TTR), direction=longer indicates better outcome; for PK parameters, direction=higher indicates higher exposure.

你是一名临床试验终点预测与循证医学分析专家。

你的任务是：基于知识截止日期之前公开可获得的证据，预测临床试验指定终点的结果。

规则：
1. 这是预测任务，不是结果检索任务。
2. 即使直接证据不足，也必须尽力给出预测。
3. 证据不足时，应降低 confidence，并明确说明不确定性，但不能仅因为证据不足而拒绝预测。
4. 只有在终点定义缺失、终点无法识别或预测目标无法映射时，才使用 not_evaluable。
5. 不得使用知识截止日期之后公开的信息。
6. 不得把试验状态、论文发表、药物批准或模型评分直接视为终点成功证据。
7. 每个 endpoint_id 必须单独预测。
8. 每个治疗组、时间点和统计目标必须单独保留。
9. 不要输出隐藏思维链或内部逐步推理过程。
10. 但必须输出完整、可公开审计的证据分析，包括证据来源、证据类型、证据与预测之间的联系以及主要不确定性。
11. 引用必须是真实使用过的公开来源 URL；没有真实 URL 时，不要声称有引用。
12. 如果无法确认某个数值，应给出基于证据的预测值，并在 uncertainty 和 rationale 中说明不确定性；不要凭空声称已经观察到该结果。
13. 证据来源必须可追溯：只有当前会话工具成功返回的公开记录、正文片段和 URL 才能称为“已检索证据”。工具返回 returned=0、source_unavailable 或空 results 时，不得把该来源当作证据。
14. 如果提到模型既有知识中的外部试验或论文，但当前会话没有成功检索并冻结其内容，必须明确标注为“未核验背景先验/假设”，不得写入 search_verification，也不得伪装成已查到的引用。
15. 当注册库和文献检索均失败或均无结果时，仍需完成可映射终点的预测，但必须显著降低 confidence（通常不高于 0.30），明确说明证据缺口；不得把试验设计、分组、样本量写成检索所得事实，只能使用动态装载的试验上下文。
16. 每条外部资料在使用前必须核对人群、药物/剂量、适应证、endpoint定义、测量单位、时间点、对照组和estimand。完全匹配的资料才可支持精确数值；同药物或相近人群资料通常只能支持方向或范围。
17. 不同药物、不同适应证、明显不同人群或不同endpoint的资料只能作为机制/背景资料，不能复制其精确效应量、置信区间或成功概率。明显不匹配的资料必须标记为 rejected_mismatch，并排除出核心证据链。
18. 对每条重要资料说明 evidence_role：direct_numeric、indirect_direction、mechanism_background 或 rejected_mismatch，并说明 mismatch_reason 和 numeric_use_allowed。没有匹配数字锚点时仍须预测已定义终点，但要扩大不确定性、降低confidence并说明外推距离；不能仅因证据间接而使用 not_evaluable。
19. 如果动态装载的试验上下文已经包含设计、组别、endpoint、时间点、人群和统计字段，不需要搜索NCT；只有字段缺失或有歧义时才允许最多一次registry_record用于设计核实。不得搜索NCT结果替代结局证据，也不得使用截止日后的注册结果。

Abstract PURPOSE Patients with transplantation-ineligible relapsed/refractory (R/R) diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) fare poorly, with limited treatment options. The antibody-drug conjugate polatuzumab vedotin targets CD79b, a B-cell receptor component. METHODS Safety and efficacy of polatuzumab vedotin with bendamustine and obinutuzumab (pola-BG) was evaluated in a single-arm cohort. Polatuzumab vedotin combined with bendamustine and rituximab (pola-BR) was compared with bendamustine and rituximab (BR) in a randomly assigned cohort of patients with transplantation-ineligible R/R DLBCL (primary end point: independent review committee [IRC] assessed complete response [CR] rate at the end of treatment). Duration of response, progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS) were analyzed using Kaplan–Meier and Cox regression methods. RESULTS Pola-BG and pola-BR had a tolerable safety profile. The phase Ib/II pola-BG cohort (n = 27) had a CR rate of 29.6% and a median OS of 10.8 months (median follow-up, 27.0 months). In the randomly assigned cohort (n = 80; 40 per arm), pola-BR patients had a significantly higher IRC-assessed CR rate (40.0% v 17.5%; P = .026) and longer IRC-assessed PFS (median, 9.5 v 3.7 months; hazard ratio [HR], 0.36, 95% CI, 0.21 to 0.63; P < .001) and OS (median, 12.4 v 4.7 months; HR, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.24 to 0.75; P = .002; median follow-up, 22.3 months). Pola-BR patients had higher rates of grade 3-4 neutropenia (46.2% v 33.3%), anemia (28.2% v 17.9%), and thrombocytopenia (41% v 23.1%), but similar grade 3-4 infections (23.1% v 20.5%), versus the BR group. Peripheral neuropathy associated with polatuzumab vedotin (43.6% of patients) was grade 1-2 and resolved in most patients. CONCLUSION Polatuzumab vedotin combined with BR resulted in a significantly higher CR rate and reduced the risk of death by 58% compared with BR in patients with transplantation-ineligible R/R DLBCL. INTRODUCTION Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) represents approximately 25% of all newly diagnosed patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma. 1 , 2 Although DLBCL is often curable, 30%-40% of patients are refractory to, or relapse after treatment with, rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone (R-CHOP) chemo-immunotherapy, the current standard of care. 3 , 4 Higher treatment failure rates are observed in poor-risk subgroups, including activated B-cell–like (ABC) and MYC/BCL2 double-expressor lymphomas (DEL). 5 , 6 Platinum-based salvage therapy followed by high-dose chemotherapy and autologous stem-cell transplantation (ASCT) can cure 30%-40% of patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) disease able to undergo this therapy. 7 , 8 However, prognosis is poor for most patients with R/R DLBCL who are ineligible for ASCT because of age, comorbidity, or inadequate response to salvage chemotherapy and for those who relapse after ASCT, with a median overall survival (OS) of approximately 6 months. 8 Currently, there is no standard of care in this setting, and treatment options include gemcitabine and/or platinum-based therapies, as well as bendamustine and rituximab (BR). 9 Recently, CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy was approved for use in the third-line or later setting in the United States and Europe. 10 , 11 Although CAR T-cell therapy appears promising, generalized use is restricted by lack of effective bridging therapies, treatment toxicity, and limited access because of high cost and need for specialized centers. Therefore, significant unmet medical need remains for patients with transplantation-ineligible R/R DLBCL, including those who experienced ASCT treatment failure. Polatuzumab vedotin is a CD79b-targeted antibody-drug conjugate delivering monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), a microtubule inhibitor. 12 , 13 CD79b is a signaling component of the B-cell receptor located on normal B cells and most mature B-cell malignancies, including > 95% of DLBCL. 14 , 15 Polatuzumab vedotin demonstrated encouraging activity in R/R DLBCL as monotherapy 16 and combined with an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, 17 yielding overall response rates (ORRs) of 13%-56%. However, complete response (CR) rates are low (0%-15%), prompting combination with additional agents. BR has been evaluated in patients with transplantation-ineligible R/R DLBCL, with median progression-free survival (PFS) of 3.6-6.7 months. 18 , 19 Given the limited treatment options in this setting, combining polatuzumab vedotin with BR (pola-BR) was considered rational and avoided the risk of overlapping neurotoxicity that could occur with platinum-based regimens. Obinutuzumab, an alternative CD20-targeted agent designed to promote greater antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and increased direct B-cell death compared with rituximab, 20 , 21 was considered a promising agent to evaluate in combination with polatuzumab vedotin and bendamustine. However, this trial was designed before availability of GOYA trial (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT01287741 ) results, when obinutuzumab combinations in DLBCL were of greater interest. 3 We report a phase Ib/II trial evaluating polatuzumab vedotin combined with bendamustine and obinutuzumab (pola-BG), and of pola-BR versus BR alone, in transplantation-ineligible R/R DLBCL, including patients who experienced treatment failure with prior ASCT. Results from a cohort of patients with follicular lymphoma (FL) will be reported separately. METHODS Trial Conduct This international, multicenter, open-label, phase Ib/II trial (GO29365; ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT02257567 ), approved by the institutional review board at each participating site, was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and the International Conference on Harmonisation guidelines for Good Clinical Practice. All patients provided written informed consent. The study was designed with input from investigators and sponsored by Genentech and F. Hoffmann-La Roche. All authors reviewed the data, vouch for the completeness and accuracy of the results and the trial’s fidelity to the Protocol, reviewed the manuscript, and agreed on its submission for publication. Editorial support was funded by F. Hoffmann-La Roche. Patients Patients aged ≥ 18 years were eligible if they had biopsy-confirmed R/R DLBCL (excluding transformed lymphoma) after ≥ 1 prior line of therapy, an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0-2, grade ≤ 1 peripheral neuropathy (PN), and were considered transplantation ineligible by the treating physician or experienced treatment failure with prior ASCT. Double- and triple-hit lymphomas were not excluded. Complete eligibility and exclusion criteria are available in the Protocol. Trial Design The phase Ib safety run-in included 6 pola-BR–treated patients and 6 pola-BG–treated patients ( Fig 1A ). The phase II portion included an expansion cohort evaluating pola-BG (21 patients) and a randomly assigned cohort (80 patients: 40 per treatment arm) comparing pola-BR with BR alone, stratified by duration of response (DOR) to last prior therapy (≤ 12 months v > 12 months; Fig 1A ). analysis_trace: Trial Identification: NCT06667687 is a Phase 1 first-in-human study of ABBV-291, a CD79b-targeting ADC with topoisomerase I inhibitor payload, in relapsed/refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Status: Active, not recruiting. Expected completion: April 2027.
Patient Population: Adults with R/R B-NHL (DLBCL, FL, MCL) after ≥2 prior lines. ECOG 0-1. Heavily pretreated population with limited options.

Target Mechanism: CD79b is validated target (expressed >95% DLBCL). ABBV-291 uses topoisomerase I inhibitor payload (different from MMAE used in polatuzumab vedotin). Preclinical data suggest best-in-class potential with potentially lower neuropathy rates.

Evidence Sources: (1) ClinicalTrials.gov protocol snapshot retrieved 2026-08-20 - trial design only; (2) Polatuzumab vedotin Phase 1/2 data (Sehn et al. JCO 2020) - CD79b ADC in similar population; (3) DCDS0780A Phase 1 data (CCR 2022) - THIOMAB CD79b ADC; (4) SHR-A1912 Phase 1 data (ASCO 2024) - CD79b ADC with topoisomerase I inhibitor.

Evidence Role Assessment: Polatuzumab and DCDS0780A provide indirect_direction for safety/tolerability and efficacy ranges. SHR-A1912 provides indirect_direction as same payload class (topoisomerase I inhibitor). No direct_numeric evidence for ABBV-291 outcomes available.

Safety Endpoints (primary-0 to primary-4): Phase 1 dose-escalation studies typically observe high AE rates (>90%). Polatuzumab vedotin showed peripheral neuropathy (43.6% any grade), neutropenia (46% G3-4). DCDS0780A showed ocular toxicity and thrombocytopenia. ABBV-291's topoisomerase I payload may have different toxicity profile - less neurotoxicity but potential GI/hepatic effects.

Efficacy Endpoints (primary-5 ORR): Polatuzumab monotherapy ORR 13-56% in R/R DLBCL. DCDS0780A ORR ~30% at RP2D. SHR-A1912 showed promising activity. Predict ORR 25-45% for ABBV-291 given same target, different payload.
PK Endpoints (secondary-3 to secondary-6): Standard ADC PK parameters expected. No direct evidence available; predictions based on typical ADC profiles.

Key Uncertainties: (1) No published ABBV-291 clinical results as of cutoff; (2) Dose escalation ongoing - final RP1ED not established; (3) Topoisomerase I payload safety profile in this population unknown; (4) Small sample size (n=21) limits precision.
Failure Risks: Dose-limiting toxicities may limit escalation; unexpected toxicity profile; insufficient efficacy at tolerable doses.

Direction Mapping: For rate endpoints (AE, DLT, ORR), direction=higher indicates higher rate; for time-to-event (DOR, PFS, TTR), direction=longer indicates better outcome; for PK parameters, direction=higher indicates higher exposure.
